guard_admission.enforced_by: code_review_bundle_guard.admission_exit_code, called by the runner AFTER the test session and INDEPENDENTLY of its result. A library can catch a refusal, substitute a fallback and let every test pass -- which is what retired N14-BUNDLE-010 -- so the exit code is not inferred from the test outcome.
guard_admission.first_initialization_tracking: ATTEMPTED at lifecycle START, not on completion. A module key is marked the moment its first eligible extent begins, so the extent that ends by RAISING has still spent the module's one chance. Reload, re-import, a retry after a failed initialisation, and any later call into an initialised module are all outside the extent.
guard_admission.native_resolution_extent: ctypes.* stays denied as a family, with one extent carved out: ctypes.dlopen and ctypes.dlsym are permitted only while a pinned RUNTIME module runs its FIRST normal initialisation on this thread, only when every Python frame between the call and that initialisation is runtime code or the interpreter's own import machinery, and only when the library resolves into the runtime tree or a protected system location.
guard_admission.not_claimed: co_filename is writable by code that builds its own code objects, so in-process adversarial code can forge RUNTIME provenance. That is the boundary the project already ratified (L6 R18) and this does not move it. What it does defend against is a refusal that changes execution semantics and is then absorbed by the caller.
guard_admission.prescribed_negative_controls: each sealed control DECLARES the refusal it is about to cause, before causing it, through guard.expect(event, contains, prescribed_by, why). The guard attributes every refusal against those declarations; anything unmatched is UNEXPECTED.
guard_admission.protected_system_locations: System32 and SysWOW64 under the SystemRoot read from HKLM through winreg -- not from the SystemRoot environment variable, for the same reason the review workspace stopped reading TMP.
guard_admission.provenance_source: WHERE CODE WAS LOADED FROM. A name supplied by executing code is not provenance, and generated or unregistered code -- anything without a real load location -- acquires none.
guard_admission.runtime_tree_untouched: the loader wrapping is an in-process wrapper on three importlib loader classes. No file in N14-RUNTIME-001 changes, and the runtime still re-hashes all 12002 of its own files at launch.
guard_admission.stop_condition: NOT 'a guard denial exists'. STOP on a launcher/runtime refusal, on a non-empty unexpected_denials, on a non-empty missing_prescribed_denials, or on an expected denial whose declaration does not match what happened.
guard_admission.thread_scope: extents are thread-local; a new thread inherits none. The attempted set is process-wide, because sys.modules is.

body: This is stated here, in its own section, because burying it in a
target cell would be the same narrowing the previous delivery was
corrected for.
Your F02 RESIDUAL named two things: the missing bounded K retry,
and the missing 2B arms for seeds 13 and 31. **Only the first was
repaired.** The Owner's residual authorization restated the F02
residual as the K doubling -- 'the current runner stops after
K/2K; the authorized second doubling to 4K is missing; no 8K
expansion is required' -- and declared that restatement
authoritative for the remediation. The builder implemented that
and stopped there.
The open half is mechanically checkable in one place and the
builder is not asking you to take its word for it:
`tree/src/itsf/mc/mc_runner.py::_execute` still constructs
`double_B` with `seed=base_seed` only, and `seed_runs` builds one
arm per governed seed at `B_WORLDS_FROZEN`. Seeds 13 and 31
therefore still run base B alone.
**Record F02 however that leaves it.** If the frozen authority
requires both halves for closure, F02 is NOT_CLOSED and the
builder expects that answer; `CLOSED_WITH_RESERVATION` exists if
you judge the K half closed and want to say so precisely. What
would be wrong is closing F02 because this package only asked
about half of it.

body: `tests/test_n14_round2_repairs.py` is both the focused evidence
for the FIRST repair and the home of the four non-regression
controls, and the residual repair changed it. Saying so is the
point: a control you cannot trust is not a control.
It changed in exactly three places, all inside F02 and F04 tests:
* `test_F02_the_final_grid_status_is_the_AND_across_every_seed`
now reads `witness_chain_by_seed` where it read
`witness_digest_by_seed` -- the field was replaced by the
attempt chain.
* `test_F02_a_non_converged_seed_is_conjunctive_for_every_seed`
now builds chains rather than single witnesses, and gives the
non-converged seed the second attempt rule (e) authorizes.
* `test_F04_test_only_grid_evidence_is_recorded_in_the_seal` was
replaced by `test_F04_the_seal_records_the_grid_evidence_kind`,
and its assertion INVERTED from `test_only is True` to
`test_only is False`. That is a direct consequence of the F04
repair: the harness runs a production-shaped prepared input, so
the authority that now matches it is the production one. The
old assertion encoded the very pairing you found admissible.
**No F01, F03, F05 or F07 test function was touched.** The check
is `git diff` between the two repair commits over that file, and
both trees are pinned in section 1 -- but you do not have a
repository here, so the checkable form is this: read the four
control test bodies in `tree/tests/test_n14_round2_repairs.py`
against the F01/F03/F05/F07 BASIS sections in
`frozen/verify002/VERIFICATION_FINDINGS.md` and judge whether
they still assert what you verified. If a control test has been
weakened to accommodate a residual repair, that is a REGRESSED
control and it fails this verification.

body: Unchanged from the delivery you last ran, and repeated because it
is the one piece of contract wording that had to be corrected
before that dispatch.
A NEW concrete blocker that this residual repair caused or
exposed, in the F02 / F04 / F06 / R1 seams it directly changed,
**affects the overall result**. It does not go in a footnote and
it is not separated from the outcome. R1 is the precedent: it was
raised exactly this way against the previous repair and it is why
F06 did not close.
An observation that is genuinely unrelated -- pre-existing,
elsewhere in the tree, or reachable only by widening the search
-- goes in a clearly separated section and does NOT affect
closure. The line is mechanical: did this repair introduce it, in
a seam this repair changed.

verification_targets.builder_claim: Residual (i) only. The witness minter used to pin the base arm to the frozen k and refuse anything else with `grid_replay_k_per_seed_not_frozen`, so the authorized second comparison was not merely unexercised -- it was inexpressible. It now admits `k = frozen x 2^d` for `0 <= d < max_doublings` and records `doublings_at_base`; `_attempt` performs ONE authorized comparison; `_witness` loops while the seed has not converged and breaks at the ruled bound; the standing is minted from every seed's full attempt chain and consumes each chain's LAST attempt; a chain that continues past a convergence is refused with `grid_convergence_retry_after_convergence`, so the bound is not a budget. The outer `double_K` RunEvidence is still produced at the frozen scales, so the K arm binds to each chain's FIRST attempt while the grid standing comes from the last.
verification_targets.builder_declared_incompleteness: RESIDUAL (ii) IS NOT REPAIRED AND IS NOT CLAIMED TO BE. `_execute` still builds `double_B` at the base seed only; seeds 13 and 31 still run base B alone. The Owner's residual authorization restated the F02 residual as the missing bounded K doubling -- 'the current runner stops after K/2K; the authorized second doubling to 4K is missing; no 8K expansion is required' -- and declared that restatement authoritative for this remediation. The builder implemented that and nothing wider. This is a scope fact, not a closure claim, and it is stated here rather than left for you to rediscover.
verification_targets.closure_requires: BOTH residuals, judged separately and named separately. For (i): a governed seed whose K-vs-2K comparison does not converge must actually run the authorized 2K-vs-4K comparison, each seed independently, stopping at the ruled bound and never beyond it; and the standing that reaches the seal must be the one taken from the FINAL attempt, so a seed still non-converged at the bound carries NON_CONVERGED into the cross-seed conjunction. For (ii): the required 2B arms for seeds 13 and 31. The builder states plainly below that (ii) was NOT repaired and why; do not let this restatement narrow the finding -- `frozen/round2/INITIAL_FINDINGS.md` and `frozen/verify002/VERIFICATION_FINDINGS.md` are authoritative over it.
verification_targets.frozen_finding: Round 2 froze this as: integration used the base seed despite constructing multiple witnesses, and omitted required doubled-scale checks and retry across the governed seed set. Your VERIFY-002 return accepted the first half as repaired -- all three seeds now reach the outcome -- and left TWO residuals standing: (i) `_witness` always executes only doublings 0 and 1 and then returns, so the authorized second K comparison is never made even though `max_doublings` is 2; and (ii) `_execute` requests a `double_B` arm only at the base seed, so seeds 13 and 31 run only base B, against M10's 3 x {B,2B}.

write_surfaces.base_is_not_a_read_root: the guard admits the frozen CHILD and nothing else outside the bundle and the runtime. The supplied base is stat'd, never listed: no sibling enumeration, no unrelated read, no part of it usable as review input.
write_surfaces.bytecode: sys.dont_write_bytecode is set by the runner itself, so nothing is written into the sealed tree or the runtime even if the runner is invoked without the launcher's -B.
write_surfaces.child_is_fresh: the child must not exist. It is refused even if it exists EMPTY, is never reused, and is never deleted by the runner: an empty directory is not evidence that it is unused, and removing another attempt's directory is worse than refusing.
write_surfaces.ephemeral_scratch: <review output root>/.scratch/ -- a dot directory beside the returns, never inside them. pytest's basetemp is pinned into it.
write_surfaces.forbidden_workspace_roots_note: DECLARED here because a sealed object cannot derive them from its own location. The sealed delivery, the review-delivery directory it sits in and the portable runtime beside it are DERIVED at runtime instead, so they stay correct if the delivery moves. Overlap is refused in both directions: a base inside one of these would put reviewer output in a governed place, and a base containing one would put a governed place inside the writable surface.
write_surfaces.output_binding: OUTPUT_BINDING.json in the child names REVIEW_ID, MANIFEST_SHA256, RUNTIME_MANIFEST_SHA256 and the substantive round. The runner refuses a workspace bound to any other review object, so one delivery's artifacts cannot be read as another's. The absolute path is execution provenance and is deliberately NOT part of the review identity: two seats may run this delivery at different paths and review the same bytes.
write_surfaces.read_boundary: the output root is an OUTPUT surface only. The guard admits that one directory and nothing else outside the bundle and the runtime, so temp siblings cannot be enumerated, read, or used as an input source.
write_surfaces.review_output_root: EXPLICITLY SUPPLIED BY THE DISPATCHER, never discovered. run_review.cmd requires --review-output-base <authorized writable base> and passes it to the runner, which canonicalises it, proves it is disjoint in BOTH directions from every forbidden root, creates exactly one FRESH child <base>/itsf-review/<REVIEW_ID>-<first 12 of MANIFEST_SHA256>, and proves CREATE/WRITE/RENAME/DELETE there by performing them. No default, no fallback, no environment read, no known folder, no profile inference: a missing parameter is a DELIVERY FAILURE before the guard arms. No username and no absolute workspace path enters the contract.
